A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. Their text, equations, figures, and complete appendices A–C are readable, and retained material can be matched despite pagination and figure-number changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original Rosenbrock optimization and CIFAR-10 training experiments, including gradient norms and componentwise quantization errors.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds second-moment sensitivity results and nanoGPT training and validation results on OpenWebText.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–3 retain the same quantized training framework and Adam/Muon update rules. Appendix C.1 retains the same mantissa-based quantization emulation. The added nanoGPT configurations concern evaluation, not a revised proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: v2 adds language-model training on OpenWebText using nanoGPT, extending coverage beyond Rosenbrock optimization and CIFAR-10 classification. This introduces a substantially different data domain and task; the original coverage remains.

E2.justification: Existing experiments retain Adam and Muon. The new nanoGPT comparison explicitly names AdamW, but v1 already discusses Adam with decoupled weight decay and reports experimental weight decay without specifying its implementation. The PDFs do not establish whether AdamW represents a new comparator variant or clearer naming.

E3.justification: v2 adds a separate nanoGPT protocol with a 512-token context, effective batch size 128, up to 10,000 iterations, and training/validation loss evaluation. It also adds second-moment-only quantization with FP32 controls and a beta2 sweep. Previously reported Rosenbrock and CIFAR-10 settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's joint component-precision sweeps, v2 Figure 7 isolates Adam's second moment, varying mantissa lengths 1, 2, 4, 7, and 10 and beta2 from 0.99 to 0.999999. This adds a controlled investigation of the central claim that beta2 approaching one amplifies quantization sensitivity.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty bands. The added trajectories do not introduce a different statistical reporting practice.

E6.justification: Existing Rosenbrock and CIFAR-10 curves are unchanged. New Figure 7 reports increased residual gradient norms near beta2=1 under second-moment quantization. Figures 12–13 add nanoGPT loss trajectories, including lower low-precision validation losses for Muon than AdamW under their respective configurations. These are new results, not improvements over matched v1 runs.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 adds explicit infimum definitions for componentwise relative-error constants. Appendix A.2 corrects an intermediate Taylor remainder from O(T^2 x^2) to O(T^3 x^2). Theorem 4.5 makes an existing asymptotic remainder calculation explicit; the principal convergence rates, assumptions, and proof structure remain.

C1.justification: The abstract and main contributions retain the same claims: convergence of fully quantized Adam/Muon, logarithmic precision scaling, and greater sensitivity of Adam's weights and second moments. Additional experiments support these retained claims without introducing a new core contribution.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly acknowledges the gap between increasing-bit guarantees and practical fixed precision, leaving the empirical sufficiency of moderate fixed precision unresolved. It replaces v1's assertion that experiments confirm logarithmic-bit sufficiency with more specific empirical interpretations, and expands applicability limits to nonsmooth, constrained/composite problems and other optimizers.

D1.justification: Appendix C.4 supplies a substantial new nanoGPT recipe: architecture, weight tying, corpus token count, gradient accumulation/clipping, optimizer learning rates and decay, Nesterov/Newton–Schulz settings, and parameter allocation between Muon and auxiliary AdamW. Existing experimental and quantizer details are retained.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning against prior quantization theory. It identifies Ozkara et al. (2025) as the closest analysis and contrasts its weight-update-only, beta1=0 setting with recursive full-state quantization. It also adds discussions of Markov et al. (2023), Hou et al. (2019), and broader optimization settings.

P1.justification: The main section and proof-appendix organization is retained. Changes include targeted explanatory additions, rewritten empirical-validation and limitations paragraphs, renaming C.3 to CIFAR-10 Experiments, and adding C.4 for nanoGPT. There is no extensive narrative restructuring.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands visual evidence with the multipanel sensitivity Figure 7 and nanoGPT Figures 12–13. All ten original graphics retain their plotted content; some are relocated or regrouped, and v1 Figures 7–10 become v2 Figures 8–11.

improvement.justification: The targeted second-moment experiment and small language-model evaluation strengthen empirical support for existing claims. Closer prior-work comparisons and explicit fixed-precision limitations improve calibration. The core guarantees remain essentially unchanged, while differing optimizer learning rates and parameter-update allocations limit how strongly the new comparison establishes intrinsic robustness.
